description: To stop sleeping and become conscious.
example: I usually wake up at six, even on weekends.

description: To physically leave your bed after waking up.
example: I wake up early, but it takes me ten minutes to get out of bed.

description: To press the button that delays your alarm for a few more minutes.
translation: Darle al botón de posponer la alarma.
example: I hit the snooze button three times this morning.

description: To prepare yourself before going somewhere.
example: It takes me about twenty minutes to get ready for work.

description: To quickly wash your face and hands to feel clean and awake.
example: Give me a minute to freshen up before we leave.

description: To wash your whole body under running water.
example: I take a shower right after the gym.

description: To put your clothes on.
example: I get dressed while my coffee is brewing.

description: To eat something small and fast in the morning.
example: I usually grab a quick breakfast before heading out.

description: To prepare coffee.
example: The first thing I do every morning is make coffee.

description: To start going in the direction of your workplace.
example: I head to work at around seven thirty.

description: To travel regularly between your home and your workplace.
example: I commute to work by car, and it takes about forty minutes.

description: To go out to do small necessary tasks, like shopping or paying bills.
example: I run errands on Saturday mornings so my Sunday stays free.

description: To arrive at your workplace.
example: I get to work around eight and start with my emails.

description: To stop working for a short time to rest.
example: I take a short break every couple of hours to clear my head.

description: To quickly get something to eat at midday.
translation: Ir por algo de comer al mediodía.
example: Do you want to grab some lunch around one?

description: To keep working after your normal finishing time.
example: I had to work late because we were closing a release.

description: To arrive at your house.
example: I usually get home a little after six.

description: To stop feeling tense and start enjoying yourself.
example: Playing games with my friends is how I unwind.

description: To wash the plates, glasses and cutlery after a meal.
example: I cook and my brother does the dishes.

description: To put things back in order so a place looks neat.
example: I tidy up a bit before going to bed.

description: To do something you did not have time to do earlier.
example: I use my weekends to catch up on sleep and messages.

description: To move through content on your phone without a clear purpose.
translation: Estar pasando el dedo por el celular sin rumbo.
example: I scroll through my phone way too much before bed.

description: To look at the alerts your apps have sent you.
example: I check my notifications once in the morning and once at night.

description: To go to bed much later than usual.
example: I stayed up late working on my personal project.

description: To get into bed in order to sleep.
example: I try to go to bed before eleven on weekdays.

word: TO GET A GOOD NIGHT'S SLEEP
pronunciation: tu guet a gud náits slip
description: To sleep well for a full night.
example: I think much better when I get a good night's sleep.

description: To sleep later than usual because you choose to.
example: On Sundays I like to sleep in until ten.

description: British expression for staying in bed longer than usual in the morning.
translation: Quedarse un rato más en la cama por la mañana.
example: I'm having a lie-in tomorrow; I don't have to work.
